title: Portable consensus-invocation contract so /work and /outcome can call the panel team-execution proved
idea: team-execution's review-revise consensus (consensus-protocol.md Step B3) is the fleet's proven defect-catcher, but it is trapped inside one plugin's Step B3 prose: no other lifecycle stage can invoke it as a primitive, so saga /work reaches for a DIFFERENT protocol (/code-review's P0/P1 findings gate) and /outcome leaves run their own verify. Extract a stable 'Consensus Invocation Contract' section — declared inputs (participants, threshold-profile, governance-mode) and outputs (verdict + persisted evidence) — that any stage invokes without re-deriving the cycle, reusing the existing recommend_execution_backend team-execution routing as the transport. This makes consensus a callable capability rather than a copy-paste pattern, and gives saga /work a real gated-consensus backend instead of a second review shape. Portability is the whole point of the theme: the value must travel out of team-execution intact.

No new plugin is created (avoids {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} burden); the contract lives in existing team-execution + saga references.

Verified by a doc-lint test asserting both /work and /outcome-leaf reference the contract anchor and that the contract enumerates the three declared inputs.

title: Single-source the consensus threshold constants that are hand-copied into ~24 reviewer prompts
idea: The acceptance math (>= 9.0 overall, < 7.0 blocking, < 5.0 severe, max 3 iterations) is not defined once — it is retyped as prose into every reviewer agent and every reference file, so changing the bar means a 20-plus-file hand-edit and guarantees the exact contract-mirror-drift disease the journal already logged. Extract one canonical consensus-thresholds reference and rewrite each reviewer's ACCEPT/BLOCKING/SEVERE line to cite it symbolically ('apply the thresholds in consensus-thresholds.md') rather than inline a literal. Add a drift-guard test asserting no bare 9.0/7.0/5.0/max-3 literal appears in any reviewer frontmatter or reference except the canonical file. This is the precondition for T5-F1-5's tunable profiles: you cannot vary a constant that is smeared across 24 files.

title: Carry gated-vs-advisory as a mode field on the consensus artifact so the split survives porting
idea: The governance split lives ENTIRELY on saga's side (operator-choice.md / recommend_execution_backend) and is enforced by forking to two different engines — gated to team-execution, advisory to ultracode's judge-panel — so team-execution's protocol has no concept of 'advisory' at all and cannot express a record-don't-block run. That means the superior named-reviewer roster is only reachable in gated mode; an operator who wants an advisory second opinion is forced into ultracode's shape, and if consensus is ported to any new stage the split does not travel with the protocol. Make consensus_mode (gated|advisory) a first-class field on the invocation contract and give consensus-protocol.md an 'Advisory mode' path: same scoring, verdict recorded as advisory-evidence, never sets a blocking gate on Step B4. Claude stays verifier-of-record in both modes, so this preserves the split's essence (does the verdict need to stick) while decoupling it from the engine fork.
basis: operator-choice.md:81-95 defines the split saga-side and routes advisory to cc-workflows-ultracode, gated to team-execution; consensus-protocol.md contains zero mention of advisory/gated (grep = 0 hits) — the downstream executor is blind to the mode. Engages the binding {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} directly (its 'must survive porting' revisit is the theme mandate) and keeps advisory Claude-reconciled, consistent with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus_mode field to the team-execution handoff schema (worker-manifest.md) and an 'Advisory mode' section to consensus-protocol.md; a test asserting advisory mode never emits a blocking gate and gated mode still does. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: Fix the 3-cycle terminal action: a gated consensus that fails to converge must HALT, not silently ship
idea: The 3-cycle cap has a governance contradiction baked into the docs: consensus-protocol.md says 'proceed with the best available version regardless of scores', while the README and the validator path say 'escalate to the user'. Under the gated contract ('the verdict must BLOCK a merge/deploy'), proceed-with-best silently ships sub-9.0 code — the gate is a paper gate. Fork the cap's terminal action on governance mode: gated -> HALT + escalate with evidence (mirroring the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade rule), advisory -> proceed-with-best-and-record (which is fine because nothing was blocking). This also reconciles the three drifted docs into one behavior. It is a near-standalone quick-win: even before T5-F1-3's mode field lands, gated is today's default and the only mode reaching team-execution, so the fix is to make the default terminal action HALT.
basis: Direct contradiction: consensus-protocol.md:17 + :61 'proceed with the best available version regardless of scores' vs README.md:99 'before escalating to the user' vs validator-execution-order.md:30 'escalate to the user' vs operator-choice.md:86 gated = 'must BLOCK a merge/deploy and PERSIST'. Engages {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} (terminal action forks on mode) and the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade principle (grounding section 2).
outcome_shape: PR rewriting the 'After 3 Cycles' section of consensus-protocol.md to fork on mode (gated->HALT+escalate, advisory->proceed+record) and reconciling README.md:99 + validator-execution-order.md:30; a test asserting a gated cycle-3 non-convergence returns HALT/escalate, not COMPLETE. Verified via that test + CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace.json bump.
dod_sketch: Merged: consensus-protocol.md 'After 3 Cycles' forks on mode (gated->HALT+escalate, advisory->proceed+record) with README.md and validator-execution-order.md reconciled; test asserts a gated cycle-3 non-convergence returns HALT/escalate, not COMPLETE.

title: Risk-tiered threshold profiles set by /plan, defaulting to today's 9.0/7.0/5.0
idea: A single global acceptance bar cannot be right for both a typo-fix and a payments migration: consensus cost is roughly fixed while its value scales with blast radius, so 9.0-on-everything overpays on trivia and under-demands on critical paths, with no operator lever either way. Introduce named threshold_profiles (relaxed / default / strict) where default is exactly today's 9.0/7.0/5.0/max-3 and strict raises the accept bar and the severe floor for load-bearing work. /plan sets the profile from risk signals it already computes (parse_issue.py deployment_sensitive / has_security) plus an operator confirm, and it travels on the same handoff as consensus_mode. This is distinct from the QUEUED per-teammate-effort seed — that tunes model/effort, this tunes the score gate — and it depends on T5-F1-2 having made the constants tunable in the first place.
basis: First-principles: consensus panel cost is a near-fixed function of roster size and iteration cap, independent of the change's risk; therefore a fixed acceptance threshold necessarily mismatches value on both tails (wasted rigor on trivia, insufficient rigor on high-blast-radius work). The plan already carries the right discriminators — parse_issue.py surfaces deployment_sensitive and has_security (operator-choice.md:98-100) — so a profile can be derived, not invented. Never downgrades a gated critical diff (ties to the governance split).
outcome_shape: PR adding a threshold_profile field to the plan->team-execution handoff (worker-manifest.md), a profiles table in consensus-thresholds.md with default == current numbers, and a /plan interrogation step; test that 'strict' propagates the raised accept bar and default equals 9.0/7.0/5.0. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.
dod_sketch: Merged: a threshold_profile field on the plan->team-execution handoff + a profiles table (default==9.0/7.0/5.0) derived from parse_issue risk signals; test asserts 'strict' propagates the raised accept bar and default equals current numbers.

title: An advisory external-engine reviewer slot in the panel — the 15/17 Claude+Codex synthesis, made protocol
idea: The strongest observed consensus signal in the fleet — Claude and Codex producing independent syntheses that converged 15 of 17 — was reconciled BY HAND, because there is no protocol slot for an external engine to contribute an independent review into a consensus panel; the roster is Claude-only and adding a second opinion is manual every run. Add an 'advisory external reviewer' role: spawned through the existing engine-dispatch as advisory-evidence (engine-registry.yaml verdict: advisory, verifier: claude), it produces a synthesis that enters the score-display step as a NON-scoring advisory column, which Claude reconciles into the gated verdict. The external voice can never flip consensus by itself, so Claude remains verifier-of-record. This turns a hand-reconciliation ritual into a repeatable, bounded panel member.

Verified via that never-gatekeeper test + version-surface bump.

title: Diversity-aware panel composition: port saga's judgment-selection so team-execution stops spawning reviewers that find nothing
idea: The two sibling plugins hold opposite philosophies on who sits on the panel: saga /code-review explicitly refuses 'a fixed specialist roster that re-opens reviewers that find nothing on this diff' and spawns only lenses with real work, while team-execution always spawns its 3 base reviewers regardless of the diff. The fixed roster both overpays (a security reviewer on a docs-only diff) and under-diversifies (3 correlated lenses can jointly miss a domain the diff actually needs). Port saga's judgment-selection into consensus-protocol.md — treat the base 3 as candidates, spawn those with real work on THIS diff, and add an explicit diversity-coverage check so the panel spans the domains the change touches rather than re-running the same three. Give reviewer-registry.md a 'when NOT to spawn' column so the selection rule is legible, not implicit.

Diversity, not just cost, is the frame: the risk is correlated lenses missing a domain, addressed by the coverage check.

Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: A consensus-worthiness pre-gate: decide BEFORE spawning whether the diff earns a full panel
idea: Consensus scales its cost only AFTER the fact — the re-review-scoping optimization re-runs just the sub-9.0 reviewers, but the INITIAL pass always spawns 'all reviewers in parallel' with no floor logic asking whether this change is worth any panel at all. So a 3-line README fix triggers the same 3-reviewer by up-to-3-cycle machine as a payments migration, and the only cap in the fleet (VERIFY_N_CAP=7) bounds the top, never the bottom. Add a Step B2.5 worthiness pre-gate: a cheap classifier (diff size, parse_issue.py risk signals, the active threshold_profile) picks a panel scale of none / single-lead-check / full-panel, defaulting to full-panel whenever gated risk signals are present so a security or deploy diff is never downgraded. This makes the cost of consensus proportional to blast radius while the governance split still forces the full machine where the verdict must stick.

Grounding brief section 7 finding 6 ('xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful') and the 350-450k-token recon fan-out singleton establish that unscaled full-fan-out is a live cost pain. Never downgrades a gated critical diff, honoring the governance split.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'Step B2.5 — Consensus worthiness' pre-gate to consensus-protocol.md + team-execution/SKILL.md selecting panel scale {none|single-check|full-panel} from diff size + risk signals + threshold_profile; a test that a small no-risk diff selects single-check and a deployment_sensitive diff forces full-panel. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: Make the gated-vs-advisory split un-loseable by porting: a typed gating flag every consensus record carries
idea: The governance split survives today only because humans remember it — when consensus is ported to a new plugin or a new participant kind, nothing structurally stops an external engine's score from being counted toward the 9.0 gate. Invert 'remember the rule' into 'the type system forbids the violation': give every consensus participant record a structural shape mirroring #283's AdvisoryEvidence (which has no verdict field), where engine != claude participants are constructed as advisory-only and a validator raises if any advisory record is folded into the gating average. The manual vigilance step is removed; a ported consensus loop that tries to gate on Codex fails a test at author time, not in production. This rides the exact mechanism #283 named ('the gated-vs-advisory consensus split is the mechanism this rides on', DECISIONS.md:1999).

title: Automate away the prose-edit: consensus thresholds become a .team-execution.json dial with today's values as defaults
idea: Changing consensus rigor today means editing prose in consensus-protocol.md — a code-change ceremony for what is really a per-run policy choice (a spike wants 7.0/2-iter; a payments change wants 9.5/no-cap). Because the defaults equal the hardcoded values, this is behavior-preserving and the existing text-pinning test still passes; a new test asserts the loader honors overrides and rejects out-of-band values (e.g. blocking_floor > pass_threshold).

title: Consensus off by default: no panel unless a cheap triage signal earns it
idea: The best version of the consensus step, for a 3-line typo fix, is no step — yet the lead spins a multi-reviewer, up-to-3-iteration panel regardless of change shape, and read-only fan-outs already burn 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes (grounding §7). Invert the default: consensus is OFF unless a cheap, deterministic triage function trips it, reusing the exact signal set that already gates team-execution offering (file_count>=8, phase_count>=4, has_security, has_infra, cross_repo, deployment_sensitive — DECISIONS.md:1611). Below the bar, ship with a single lead review and log 'consensus skipped: change below triage bar'; above it, run the full panel. This removes the panel as a mandatory step and scales token spend to actual risk, while leaving the operator a one-flag force-on override so the gate is never silently weakened on something that matters.

Verified: a below-bar run produces the skip log and no reviewer spawns.

title: Automate the hand-reconciliation: an advisory convergence-diff between Claude and an external synthesis

Automate that manual reconciliation into a convergence step: an external advisory reviewer runs the SAME review-criteria.md rubric independently, and the lead auto-computes a convergence-diff (dimensions where Claude and the external engine agree vs the specific divergences) surfaced as a table for the human. The external engine stays strictly advisory — its scores never enter the 9.0 gating average and it can never block completion, exactly per the chaperone-dispatch second-opinion contract. What is removed is the manual diffing labor; what is kept is the diversity signal that caught defects green suites missed (grounding §3 finding 2).

title: Collapse saga /code-review lenses and team-execution reviewers into one portable lens registry
idea: saga's /code-review selects judgment-picked review lenses and team-execution maintains its own reviewer-registry.md roster of ~14 reviewer agents with review-criteria.md rubrics — two parallel reimplementations of 'a set of review lenses scored against a rubric'. Remove the double-maintenance: extract a single portable lens registry (name, dimensions, rubric pointer, applicability precondition) that both surfaces consume, so a lens defined once (e.g. security, concurrency, api-compat) is available to both the saga review gate and the team-execution consensus panel. Porting consensus to a third surface then means pointing at the registry, not re-authoring lenses. This is the protocol-extraction axis applied to membership rather than thresholds: the review-lens roster becomes a shared primitive instead of a per-plugin copy.

title: Remove the arbitrary 3-cycle cap: stop on convergence, not on a counter
idea: The fixed 'Maximum iterations: 3, then proceed with best version regardless of scores' cap either wastes a cycle on a change that already converged at cycle 2 or guillotines a change still climbing at cycle 3. Invert the counter into a convergence test: stop when the cross-cycle score delta for every still-open reviewer falls below an epsilon (converged — no further motion) OR a hard ceiling is hit, and when the ceiling is hit escalate to the human instead of silently proceeding. The manual 'count to 3 and give up' step is replaced by measured convergence. The hard ceiling defaults to 3 so this is behavior-preserving at the boundary, and it pairs with the threshold-config seam (idea T5-F2-3) so both epsilon and ceiling are dials, not constants.
basis: First-principles: a fixed iteration count is a proxy for 'reviews have stopped improving', and the proxy is wrong in both directions — a 9.4->9.4 pair at cycles 1-2 has converged and cycle 3 is pure token waste, while an 8.0->8.6->8.9 trajectory is still climbing and cycle-3 cutoff discards a review that would have passed at cycle 4. consensus-protocol.md:61 literally says 'proceed with best version' regardless of scores, i.e. it already admits the counter is not a quality signal. Measuring inter-cycle delta directly replaces the proxy with the thing it approximates.
outcome_shape: PR editing consensus-protocol.md 'Cycle Structure' + 'After 3 Cycles' sections to a convergence-or-ceiling rule, adding convergence_epsilon + iteration_ceiling to consensus_spec.py, plus tests/test_consensus_convergence_stop.py (converged pair stops early; still-climbing trajectory hits ceiling and escalates to human, not silent proceed). Verified: a 9.4/9.4 cycle-2 run spawns zero cycle-3 reviewers.
dod_sketch: Merged: consensus-protocol.md cycle-structure rewritten to a convergence-or-ceiling rule with convergence_epsilon + iteration_ceiling in consensus_spec; test asserts a converged 9.4/9.4 cycle-2 run spawns zero cycle-3 reviewers and a still-climbing run hits the ceiling and escalates.

title: Consensus is one algebra, reimplemented three times — extract it

Reframe one level up: there is a single consensus primitive the fleet re-derives per plugin. Extract a machine-readable `consensus_spec.py` into the existing saga scripts substrate (NOT a new plugin) that names the panel/aggregate/verdict/re-review contract once, and have team-execution's SKILL and saga verify both reference it. A drift-guard test asserts the prose threshold table and the code constants stay in lockstep.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:24-62 encodes the review-revise loop as prose; execution_spec.py:111-114 encodes a parallel but separately-chosen panel bound (VERIFY_N_CAP=7) for the same 'panel of scorers' concern. Two surfaces, one algebra, zero shared definition. Honors {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by extracting into saga scripts, adding no plugin.

title: 9.0 is not a constant — it is a risk-tier function masquerading as one
idea: The protocol treats 9.0/7.0/5.0 as universal constants applied identically to a README typo and an auth-boundary rewrite. That uniformity is a hidden choice, not a law. Reframe: the acceptance threshold is a function of the change's risk-tier, resolved from the same plan metadata that already drives tier tables. A docs-only change convenes at a lower bar and lower panel; a security-touching change raises the bar and lowers the escalation floor. Encode a named threshold-profile table keyed by risk-tier and thread the resolved profile through the review cycle so the number is derived, never hardcoded.

title: The 3-cycle cap silently ships — but HALT-not-degrade is the house posture
idea: 'After 3 cycles, proceed with the best available version regardless of scores' treats forced-ship as the fixed terminal default. Reframe the cap's outcome as a configurable disposition — {ship-best, halt-and-escalate, extend-with-approval} — defaulting to halt so non-convergence surfaces rather than silently degrading a merge. The max-3 count itself becomes a floor the operator can lift with explicit approval, mirroring the attended spend-increase rule.

title: Split consensus into an advisory layer and a gated layer so porting can't leak the boundary
idea: Today 'reviewer score' and 'gate' are conflated in one flow, so every plugin that ports consensus must re-derive where advice stops and adjudication begins — the exact seam an external engine could slip a gate through. Reframe consensus as two explicit layers: an advisory-synthesis layer (any scorer, including external engines, contributes evidence) and a gated-adjudication layer (Claude verifier-of-record alone converts evidence into a verdict). Make the layer boundary a first-class artifact in the shared spec so the gated-vs-advisory governance split survives any port by construction, not by each plugin re-reading the prose.

title: Make the 15/17 Claude+Codex independent-synthesis convergence a repeatable membership mode
idea: The reviewer panel assumes membership = a set of Claude lenses scoring one shared artifact. But the fleet has proven prior art for a different, stronger consensus shape — two engines producing fully independent syntheses that converged 15/17, hand-reconciled. Reframe independent-synthesis-then-reconcile as a first-class panel membership mode, not a one-off manual event: an external engine produces a blind parallel synthesis, Claude produces its own, and Claude reconciles the divergences (advisory only, Claude adjudicates). This ports the mined win into the standing protocol.

title: Correlated lenses fake agreement — measure panel independence, don't assume it
idea: Panel membership is chosen by judgment from a fixed reviewer registry, and consensus is read off the average as if every lens were an independent vote. But two reviewers with correlated lenses (e.g. security-reviewer and privacy-reviewer overlapping on data-handling) inflate apparent agreement — the number looks like consensus when it is one viewpoint counted twice. Reframe consensus quality as a function of lens independence: annotate each reviewer's lens with its correlation neighbors and add a selection guard that flags a panel whose accepting lenses are not genuinely independent, so a 9.2 average from three correlated lenses is not treated as strong consensus.
basis: First-principles: averaging correlated scorers overstates agreement — the 15/17 convergence number is meaningful precisely because the two syntheses were independent; strip independence and the same 15/17 is uninformative. reviewer-registry.md lists lenses with no independence metadata, so overlap is invisible to the aggregator today.
outcome_shape: PR adding lens-independence/correlation annotations to reviewer-registry.md and a panel-selection guard in consensus-protocol.md that warns when accepting lenses share a correlation cluster. Verified: a panel of three correlated lenses raises the independence warning; a diverse panel does not.

title: Consensus should have to earn its convene — add an entry gate, not just exit scoping
idea: The protocol optimizes cost only on the way out (re-run only reviewers scoring <9.0) but always convenes the full panel on the way in, spending a multi-reviewer fan-out on trivial diffs. That 'always convene' is an unexamined default. Reframe: convening consensus is itself a cost decision that must clear an entry threshold on change risk/size — below it, a single-lens or no-panel path; above it, a panel whose size scales with risk. This makes consensus worth its tokens by construction and composes with the risk-tier thresholds (T5-F3-2).

Grounding-brief §7 records 350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs — evidence that unconditional fan-out is the dominant spend.

title: Two plugins picked two different bounds for the same panel-blowup fear — reconcile them

Unify it into a single bounded-panel policy in the shared consensus spec, expressing both the participant cap and the iteration cap as instances of one 'panels are bounded' rule with documented per-context values.

title: Single consensus-contract source of truth both plugins conform to
idea: Today two divergent consensus implementations exist with no shared primitive: team-execution scores dimensions 0-10 against a 9.0/7.0/5.0 rubric (consensus-protocol.md), while saga /code-review emits findings from judgment-selected lenses (code-review/SKILL.md:145-167) with no scores at all. title: Stamp the gated/advisory governance bit onto the consensus verdict artifact
idea: The gated-vs-advisory distinction currently lives only as a routing INPUT in lifecycle_state.py (consensus_is_gated selects team-execution vs the advisory ultracode branch) — it is consumed at dispatch and then lost. When a consensus verdict is later ported to a new locus (an /outcome leaf, a resumed saga, a code-review escalation), nothing on the produced artifact records whether that verdict was gating a merge or was throwaway advisory, so the governance split cannot survive the port. Stamp governance_mode (gated|advisory) plus consensus_is_gated onto the consensus verdict/completion record itself, and add a guard that refuses to treat an advisory-stamped verdict as a merge gate. This makes the split a durable property of the evidence, not a transient dispatch decision — the compounding win is that any future consumer of a consensus artifact inherits its governance semantics for free.

title: External-engine advisory reviewer slot in the consensus panel (non-scoring)

Add an advisory reviewer slot that dispatches one external engine (Codex offload, or Ollama at $0) as a non-scoring lens whose findings feed the fix-consolidation step but NEVER count toward the 9.0 consensus and never block. The panel gains a genuinely independent perspective (different model family catches what a monoculture green suite misses) while Claude stays verifier-of-record. The slot reuses the existing external-engine-workers.md chaperone-dispatch plumbing, so it is a registry entry, not new machinery — every future consensus run can opt in a second opinion for the price of one config flag.

title: One shared lens/reviewer registry feeding both consensus loci
idea: Reviewer membership is defined twice with divergent selection models: team-execution's reviewer-registry.md (keyword-triggered optional reviewers atop a fixed base 3) and saga /code-review's judgment-selected lens-catalog (4 always-on + conditional). A lens authored for one is invisible to the other, so adding e.g. a 'concurrency' or 'privacy' perspective is a two-place job that drifts. Merge them into one shared lens/reviewer registry keyed by domain-trigger, with a per-locus selection adapter (keyword-match for team-execution, judgment for code-review) reading the same catalog. Define a reviewer once, both consensus surfaces can draw on it — the compounding return grows with every lens added and eliminates a standing drift source.

Load references/lens-catalog.md'). title: A consensus-worth-it estimator that recommends inline vs advisory-N vs gated-team
idea: There is no lever telling an operator WHEN consensus earns its tokens — the choice between inline self-review, an advisory throwaway N-vote panel, and a full gated team is made ad hoc. Build a small pre-consensus estimator that takes blast radius (files touched, security surface, whether the verdict gates a merge) and the mode-dependent spend posture and outputs a recommendation with a cheaper fallback always surfaced: e.g. 'docs-only, non-gating → inline; security surface + merge gate → gated team.' It reuses the triage-escape-hatch signals already in reviewer-registry.md and the governance bit from idea 3, and encodes the intake's asymmetric-approval rule (attended spend-increases need explicit yes) as machinery rather than prose. Every future run inherits a defensible, cheap-first consensus-cost decision instead of re-litigating it.

Cache-first only silent default') and tension 4 (Fable spend lever: 'expensive never silent default') are direct operator statements demanding this lever be encoded, not hardcoded. The triage-escape-hatch qualifying criteria (reviewer-registry.md:61-76: single-config-change, no security surface, <3 files) already enumerate the blast-radius signals the estimator needs.

title: Convergence-driven iteration cap replacing the flat max-3
idea: The 'Maximum iterations: 3, then proceed with best version regardless' rule (consensus-protocol.md:17,61) wastes cycles when reviewers already agree and truncates when they are still moving. Replace the flat cap with a convergence stopping rule: stop early when inter-cycle score deltas fall below an epsilon (reviewers have stabilized) AND all pass, and allow a bounded extra cycle when scores are still climbing steeply toward the threshold — with the hard ceiling (from idea 2's max_iterations config) preserved as a backstop. This ports the 15/17 convergence concept from ad-hoc hand-reconciliation into the loop's own stopping logic, spending iterations where they change the verdict and skipping them where they don't. Compounding: the same convergence primitive later informs the advisory-N vote count and the external-slot reconciliation.
basis: First-principles: the current cap conflates a cost bound with a stopping criterion. A fixed N is optimal only if marginal iteration value is constant, but review-revise value is monotonically decreasing (each cycle resolves the largest-remaining fixes first per the consolidation/dedup step, consensus-protocol.md:131-138) and approaches zero as scores converge. A convergence test (delta < epsilon) is the correct stopping rule for a decreasing-returns sequence; a flat N either overspends past convergence or halts a still-improving sequence. The 15/17 convergence observation (section 7) is empirical evidence that independent reviewers do converge, making an epsilon-test well-defined rather than speculative.
outcome_shape: PR rewriting consensus-protocol.md's cycle-structure and after-3-cycles sections to a convergence stopping rule with a configurable epsilon and a hard max-iterations backstop, plus a simulation test over synthetic score trajectories asserting early-stop on convergence and backstop-halt on divergence; verified by the test covering a converged sequence (stops at cycle 2) and a stuck sequence (halts at ceiling).

title: Extract consensus as a Raft-style reusable module (consensus_spec.py)
idea: In distributed systems, Raft succeeded precisely because it was designed as an *understandable, extractable* consensus module that etcd, Consul, and TiKV all vendor rather than re-deriving Paxos per project. The fleet has the opposite: consensus lives only as prose in team-execution's consensus-protocol.md while saga's /code-review, /doc-review, and /founder-review each hand-roll their own scoring narrative. Extract the scoring/verdict/iteration state machine into a saga-side primitive `plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py` (a peer of execution_spec.py) that takes a panel of scored dimensions and returns {reached, blocking, re-run-set} deterministically. team-execution's consensus-protocol.md and saga review skills both consume it instead of restating the 9.0/re-run/3-cap logic. The primitive is pure and unit-testable, killing the drift where each surface's threshold wording quietly diverges.
basis: Raft (Ongaro & Ousterhout, 'In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm', 2014) was explicitly built to be reused as a library module across etcd/Consul/TiKV rather than reimplemented; the design goal was extraction. Fleet counterpart: consensus lives as prose in plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md:17,40,74 (thresholds/iteration cap) with no shared code, while grounding brief §3 item 2 records team-execution consensus catching defects green suites missed — the primitive worth extracting.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py (pure scoring/verdict/re-run state machine) + tests/test_consensus_spec.py; consensus-protocol.md rewritten to cite the primitive; version/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json bumps for saga + team-execution. Verified by unit tests asserting identical verdicts to the current prose rules on a fixture score matrix (all>=9.0 pass; any dim<7.0 forced re-run; 3-cap terminal).

title: Authority gradient: typed gating|advisory participant field (flight-deck PIC model)
idea: Aviation cockpit resource management runs a strict authority gradient: the first officer and every automated advisory (TCAS traffic callouts, EGPWS) can and must speak, but the Pilot-in-Command holds final command authority and a subordinate voice can never *execute* a clearance. Port that structurally into the extracted consensus primitive: every panel participant carries `authority: gating | advisory`, and the state machine mechanically refuses to let any advisory score move the reached/blocking outcome — advisory scores are surfaced and reconciled by Claude, never summed into the gate. This makes {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} a *typed invariant that survives porting* to any consumer, rather than a convention re-explained per plugin. A guard test asserts that flipping an advisory participant's score from 10 to 0 never changes the gate verdict.
basis: Binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283, grounding brief §2): 'Claude is verifier-of-record for every gated decision; codex/agy = generator/advisory-reviewer/non-gated worker only. Structurally enforced.' This idea IS the structural enforcement mechanism and its revisit-when ('team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot') is exactly what a typed authority field prepares for safely. Alignment note §2: 'issue text must be explicit that consensus participation is advisory-only.'
outcome_shape: PR adding an `authority` enum field to the consensus_spec.py participant schema + a guard test (test_consensus_authority_invariant.py) proving advisory-score perturbation cannot change the gate; consensus-protocol.md and external-engine-workers.md updated to mark external engines authority=advisory. Verified by the invariant test + a metadata drift test that every external-engine reviewer entry is authority=advisory.

title: SPC-style consensus profiles: control limits derived per work-class, not hardcoded
idea: Statistical process control never uses one universal control limit; the UCL/LCL are set per process from its own capability, and a tighter limit is chosen where defects are costlier. The consensus protocol instead freezes 9.0/7.0/5.0 and max-3-iterations as global constants, so a docs typo pass and a security-critical change face identical gates. Introduce named `consensus-profiles` (e.g. `strict` 9.5/8.0/2-cap, `standard` 9.0/7.0/3-cap, `advisory` 7.0/none/1-cap) selected by work-class at invocation, replacing the magic constants with a profile lookup in consensus_spec.py. The profile is an operator-choosable input, honoring the intake's 'plugins encode the question, not a hardcoded mandate' posture, and each profile ships with a documented rationale for its limits.
basis: Hardcoded constants: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3'), :40 ('ACCEPT >= 9.0'), :72 ('< 7.0 BLOCKING'), :232 ('< 5.0 severe'); execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP=7 is the only other consensus-shaped constant and is already a named tunable, establishing the pattern. Intake brief resolved-tension 1: 'plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded mandate.' Analogy: SPC control limits (Shewhart control charts) are process-derived, not universal.
outcome_shape: PR adding a CONSENSUS_PROFILES table to consensus_spec.py (or a consensus-profiles.md registry) + profile-selection param threaded through consensus-protocol.md; tests asserting each profile's gate math and that removing a profile fails a drift guard. Verified by unit tests per profile + CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bumps.

title: Diversity-floor panel composition + external advisory synthesis (wisdom-of-crowds)
idea: Scott Page's Diversity Prediction Theorem proves a crowd's collective error falls as the *diversity* of its members' models rises — accuracy alone is not enough, cognitive diversity is a first-class ingredient. The current reviewer roster is a fixed set (Devil's Advocate, Security, Architecture, Infra) with no measure of lens overlap, and the mined 15/17 Claude+Codex independent-synthesis convergence is unused machinery. Add a panel-composition step that (a) scores lens overlap across the selected reviewers against a diversity floor, warning when the panel is redundant, and (b) optionally seats one external-engine participant (Codex/DeepSeek) that produces an *independent* synthesis reconciled by Claude — advisory-only, never gating. This operationalizes the 15/17 prior art as a repeatable divergence-check, not a one-off.
basis: Scott Page, 'The Difference' (2007) Diversity Prediction Theorem: collective error = average individual error minus prediction diversity — diversity mathematically reduces error. Fleet prior art: grounding brief §7 records 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converged 15/17, hand-reconciled.' Crosses {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) — engaged by keeping the external participant authority=advisory, reconciled by Claude as verifier-of-record, matching its revisit-when for a team-execution external-engine slot; and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) second-opinion→opus/high dispatch shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding a panel-diversity check + optional external advisory synthesis slot to consensus-protocol.md and reviewer-registry.md, with the external slot marked authority=advisory (depends on T5-F5-2's typed field); a lens-overlap heuristic doc + test. Verified by a test that a redundant panel (two near-identical lenses) trips the diversity warning and that the external synthesis never enters the gate denominator.

title: Byzantine-tolerant quorum: survive one miscalibrated reviewer without weakening the gate
idea: Byzantine fault tolerance in distributed consensus assumes some participants may be arbitrarily wrong or adversarial and still reaches a correct decision with a 3f+1 quorum. The consensus protocol today demands unanimity (ALL reviewers >= 9.0), so a single miscalibrated or stuck reviewer — the Devil's Advocate is *designed* to be adversarial — can pin the panel at the 3-cycle cap even when the substance is sound. Add a quorum mode where, above a panel size, the gate tolerates up to f dissenting reviewers *provided Claude (verifier-of-record) explicitly adjudicates each dissent* — the tolerance never hands the gate to an advisory engine, it only lets Claude discount a demonstrably-miscalibrated lens with a logged justification. This keeps the gate Claude-owned while stopping one outlier from forcing a false 3-cap failure.
basis: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (Lamport, Shostak, Pease, 'The Byzantine Generals Problem', 1982; Castro & Liskov PBFT 1999): 3f+1 quorum reaches correct consensus despite f arbitrarily-faulty nodes. Fleet counterpart: consensus-protocol.md:74 requires unanimity ('ALL >= 9.0') and :17 caps at 3 cycles, so one stuck reviewer forces the documented 3-cap degrade (:161-172). Does NOT contradict {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} because adjudication stays with Claude — dissent-discounting is a Claude judgment with logged cause, not a quorum handed to an engine.
outcome_shape: PR adding an optional quorum-with-adjudication mode to consensus_spec.py/consensus-protocol.md: above panel-size K, up to f dissents may be Claude-adjudicated with a mandatory logged justification appended to the completion report. Verified by tests that adjudication requires a recorded cause and that f=0 (default) preserves today's unanimity behavior exactly.
dod_sketch: Merged: an optional quorum-with-adjudication mode in consensus_spec allowing up to f Claude-adjudicated dissents above panel-size K with a mandatory logged cause; test asserts adjudication requires recorded cause and f=0 preserves unanimity exactly.

title: Risk-based panel underwriting: size the panel to change exposure
idea: Insurance underwriting sets coverage and scrutiny proportional to expected loss — you don't run a full actuarial review on a trivial policy, and you never skip it on a catastrophic one. Consensus currently spawns the whole reviewer panel regardless of blast radius, so a one-line docs fix and a payments-path change both pay full-panel token cost. Add a consensus-worthiness pre-gate in consensus_spec.py that reads cheap risk signals already available (diff line count, files touched, security/auth path hits, public-API surface) and recommends a panel size — a single Devil's Advocate for low-exposure changes escalating to the full diverse panel plus strict profile for high-exposure ones. The recommendation is surfaced as an operator-choosable lever (never a silent downgrade), and the existing VERIFY_N_CAP=7 bounds the top end.
basis: First-principles: consensus cost scales with panel size x iterations x token-per-reviewer, yet review value is non-uniform — grounding brief §7 flags '350-450k recon' spend and §6 item 6 records operator pain that 'xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful.' execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP=7 already bounds panel size, proving panel-size-as-a-tunable is legitimate; no mechanism yet *chooses* within that bound by risk. A risk-proportional selector converts a flat cost into an expected-value-weighted one, and being operator-surfaced it honors intake tension 1 (no silent spend change).
outcome_shape: PR adding a risk-signal panel-size recommender to consensus_spec.py + consensus-protocol.md Step B3a, surfaced as an operator prompt with a documented low/standard/high mapping. Verified by unit tests mapping fixture diffs (docs-only, mixed, security-path) to recommended panel sizes and asserting the recommendation is advisory (operator can override upward).

title: Acceptance-sampling review: inspect a risk-stratified sample of hunks, not every line
idea: Manufacturing quality control abandoned 100% inspection decades ago for acceptance sampling (MIL-STD-105 / AQL): inspect a statistically-sized sample sized to lot size and acceptable quality level, and reject the lot if sample defects exceed the acceptance number. On large diffs the panel currently reasons over the whole change (or an artifact-pointer to it), and cost grows with lot size. Add an acceptance-sampling mode where reviewers are directed to a risk-stratified sample of hunks (all security/auth/public-API hunks always in-sample; the remainder sampled by an AQL-style plan sized to diff magnitude), with an explicit acceptance number — if sampled defects exceed it, the whole diff is kicked back to full review. This bounds review cost sub-linearly in diff size while keeping high-risk regions fully covered.
basis: MIL-STD-105E / ISO 2859-1 acceptance sampling: sample size and acceptance number are functions of lot size and Acceptable Quality Level; full inspection is reserved for failed lots. Fleet counterpart: consensus-protocol.md:28,190-198 already passes reviewers a full diff or artifact-pointer with no size-scaling, and grounding brief §7 records large-diff review cost as a spend driver. Stratification (security/auth always in-sample) borrows the same risk-tiering as T5-F5-6, keeping governance intact since gating still rides on Claude's read of sampled findings.
outcome_shape: PR adding an acceptance-sampling review mode to consensus-protocol.md + a hunk-sampler helper (risk-stratified, AQL-sized) with an acceptance-number escalation-to-full-review rule; tests. Verified by tests that all security/auth hunks are always in-sample, that exceeding the acceptance number triggers full-diff re-review, and that sample size grows sub-linearly with diff size.
dod_sketch: Merged: an acceptance-sampling review mode + risk-stratified AQL-sized hunk-sampler with an acceptance-number escalation-to-full-review rule; test asserts all security/auth hunks are always in-sample and sample size grows sub-linearly with diff size.

title: Consensus replay log: append-only score ledger (event-sourced, Raft-log style)
idea: Raft's correctness rests on a replicated *append-only log* — every state transition is an immutable, ordered, replayable entry, which is also what makes the cluster auditable and recoverable. Consensus today emits only a transient score table per cycle and a final prose summary; once the run ends, the per-reviewer, per-iteration score trajectory is gone, so nobody can mine reviewer calibration drift or prove chain-of-custody on a gate decision. Emit an append-only consensus ledger (one entry per reviewer per iteration: score, verdict, fix-request digest, authority, adjudication cause) written by consensus_spec.py alongside the completion report. This makes consensus decisions replayable and audit-grade, and feeds the fleet's dark learning-mining loop (theme 10) with structured reviewer-calibration data it currently lacks — directly answering the 'evidence-artifact chain-of-custody' gap.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:142-157 shows scores are rendered only as an ephemeral per-cycle table and :166-172 keeps just a final prose note — no durable per-iteration record. Grounding brief §7 names 'probe script overwriting FAIL evidence artifact later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)' as a real integrity gap, and §3 item 5 records the promote/learning loop 'has never fired' for lack of substrate. An append-only ledger is the substrate. Reinforces theme 10 (provenance discipline) from the consensus side.
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only consensus-ledger writer to consensus_spec.py (JSONL: run-id, iteration, reviewer, authority, score, verdict, fix-digest, adjudication-cause) + consensus-protocol.md wiring + tests. Verified by a test that a 3-iteration run produces a complete, ordered, immutable ledger and that re-running does not rewrite prior entries; CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bumps.
dod_sketch: Merged: an append-only JSONL consensus-ledger writer (run-id, iteration, reviewer, authority, score, verdict, fix-digest, adjudication-cause) + wiring; test asserts a 3-iteration run yields a complete ordered immutable ledger and re-run does not rewrite prior entries.

title: One consensus kernel: extract the scoring contract from prose+frontmatter into a single versioned spec
idea: Flip the constraint 'every reviewer re-declares the pass rule' to its extreme: exactly ONE place in the fleet may state a consensus threshold. Today the 9.0/7.0/5.0 rule is written five+ times — consensus-protocol.md lines 17/70-74 plus each agent body (architecture-reviewer.md:120, devils-advocate-reviewer.md:62, security-reviewer.md:64) — a guaranteed drift surface. Create a machine-readable consensus-contract.json (accept>=9.0, revise-band 7.0-8.9, blocking<7.0, severe<5.0, max_iterations=3, denominator=applicable-dimensions) that consensus-protocol.md and every reviewer agent reference by anchor instead of restating numerically. Add a drift-guard test asserting no agent body contains a bare numeric threshold literal that disagrees with the contract. The practical kernel even if 'single source' is dogmatic: kill the copy-paste threshold drift that already burned 343 cards in the validate_card_body incident (grounding brief §3).
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Each reviewer must achieve an overall score of >= 9.0/10') and :70-74 restate the threshold that is ALSO independently hardcoded in agents/architecture-reviewer.md:120, agents/devils-advocate-reviewer.md:62, agents/security-reviewer.md:64 — same rule, five authored copies, no shared source; grounding brief §3 ranks contract-mirror drift as the #1 cross-repo pain (validate_card_body stale hand-copy, 343 cards).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-contract.json + a tests/test_consensus_contract_drift.py that greps every agents/*.md and consensus-protocol.md for numeric threshold literals and fails on any that disagree with the JSON; CHANGELOG + plugin.json version bump. Verified: intentionally editing one agent's 9.0 to 8.5 turns the test red.

title: Portable consensus-verdict artifact: a JSON envelope any plugin emits and any plugin can honor
idea: Flip 'consensus lives inside team-execution's B3 loop' to the extreme where consensus is a free-floating artifact no single plugin owns. Define a consensus-verdict schema (run-id, per-lens scores, overall, verdict, gated-bit, iteration, unresolved-fixes, produced-by) that team-execution's Step B3 emits and that saga /code-review, /outcome leaf gates, and /qa can all read without re-running the panel. The kernel: consensus results today are trapped in a session transcript and a completion report; making the verdict a durable typed artifact (mirroring the artifact_pointer.py pattern already in this plugin) lets a downstream gate cite an upstream consensus instead of re-spending tokens on it, and lets the gated-bit travel with the verdict rather than being re-derived.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/artifact_pointer.py already establishes a typed JSON pointer artifact pattern in this exact plugin (CLAUDE.md notes team-execution is now hybrid because of it); consensus-protocol.md:161-172 shows the verdict currently dies as free-text in a completion report with no schema, so no downstream consumer can honor it.
outcome_shape: PR adding references/consensus-verdict-schema.md + a snapshot/deref helper in artifact_pointer.py (or a sibling script) that serializes B3 scores; consensus-protocol.md Step B3d/After-3-Cycles updated to emit the envelope; unit test round-trips a verdict and asserts the gated-bit and applicable-denominator survive serialization. Verified by the round-trip test.
dod_sketch: Merged: references/consensus-verdict-schema.md + a serialize/deref helper emitting the B3 verdict envelope; round-trip test asserts the gated-bit and applicable-denominator survive serialization.

title: Everything-advisory flip: make gated-vs-advisory a bit that rides the verdict, not a saga-side routing accident
idea: Flip to the extreme where ZERO consensus ever gates — every verdict is advisory. That world is wrong (loses the whole point of team-execution gates), but running the flip exposes the kernel: the gated/advisory distinction currently lives only saga-side in lifecycle_state.py consensus_is_gated and operator-choice.md routing, NOT in the consensus protocol itself, so a team-execution verdict carries no self-description of whether it was meant to block. Port the governance-split bit INTO the consensus artifact so any consumer knows a verdict's standing without re-reading saga's router. This explicitly preserves {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split}: the bit is not erased, it is made portable so the split survives when consensus is consumed outside saga's /plan flow (the anchor's whole intent — that a verdict must 'need to stick' — is exactly what a portable bit encodes).
basis: operator-choice.md:81-95 defines the split entirely as a backend-routing decision (consensus_is_gated=True default in lifecycle_state.py:133-area); the split is decided in saga/plan §5.2 KTD4 and never re-expressed inside team-execution's consensus-protocol.md — the verdict artifact is governance-blind, so porting consensus out of saga would silently drop the gated meaning the anchor #gated-vs-advisory... exists to protect.
outcome_shape: PR adding a required 'gated' field to the consensus-verdict envelope (from T5-F6-2), wiring saga lifecycle_state.py to stamp it at B3 emit-time, and a doc-review note in operator-choice.md that the bit is now verdict-resident not router-resident; test asserts an advisory verdict never sets the merge-block flag and a gated one always does. Verified by the paired test.

title: Plan-declared threshold profiles: flip the hardcoded 9.0/7.0/5.0 to a per-outcome consensus stringency dial
idea: Flip the constraint 'the bar is always 9.0' to its two extremes — a hotfix that only needs 5.0-to-ship, and a security-critical release that demands a clean 10.0. Neither extreme is a fixed global, which is the point: the stringency should be an operator/plan choice, not a constant baked into prose. Introduce named threshold profiles (e.g. strict=9.0/7.0/5.0, standard=8.0/6.0/4.0, ship-fast=7.0/5.0/3.0) selectable in the saga /plan unit table alongside the existing tier palette, defaulting to strict. The kernel survives even if operators never touch it: profiles turn the magic numbers into a declared, greppable, testable config instead of five hand-copied literals, and make 'why did this pass' auditable.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 and :70-78 hardcode 9.0/7.0/5.0 and max-iterations=3 as universal constants with no operator lever; saga/plan/SKILL.md already carries the ONE existing per-unit stringency table (the tier palette, plan/SKILL.md:296-352 per grounding brief §1), which is the natural host for a consensus-profile column — a lever seam that already exists.
outcome_shape: PR adding threshold-profiles to consensus-contract.json (from T5-F6-1) + a profile-selector column in plan/SKILL.md's unit table + KTD4 interrogation asking stringency when consensus is chosen; drift test asserts every profile keeps accept>=revise>=blocking>=severe ordering. Verified by the ordering test and a plan-render fixture showing the column.

title: Infinite-iterations flip: replace the max-3 cap with plateau-detection convergence
idea: Flip 'max 3 iterations, then ship best version' to unbounded iteration, then mine the kernel. Unbounded is unaffordable and can loop forever, but the fixed cap of 3 is equally arbitrary — it can stop one fix short of consensus, or waste a cycle when scores have already plateaued. Add plateau-detection: stop early when the round-over-round score delta for all still-open reviewers falls below an epsilon (no meaningful movement = a real disagreement a fourth cycle won't resolve), and surface that as 'converged-stuck' rather than the current silent 'proceeded with best version'. Keep 3 as the hard ceiling but let convergence end it sooner and label WHY it ended. This makes the termination reason a portable, honest signal instead of an opaque cap.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3. After 3 cycles, proceed with the best available version regardless of scores') and :161-172 (After 3 Cycles) treat 3 as a magic constant and the exit as undifferentiated. First-principles: a cap conflates two distinct terminal states — 'still improving but out of budget' vs 'stuck, scores not moving'. These warrant different operator actions (grant another cycle vs escalate the disagreement), so a single cap that cannot tell them apart discards decision-relevant information at exactly the moment consensus fails.
outcome_shape: PR updating consensus-protocol.md Step B3/After-3-Cycles with a plateau-epsilon rule + a 'termination_reason' field (consensus-reached | converged-stuck | cap-reached) on the verdict envelope; a small helper computing round-delta with a unit test over score sequences that plateau vs still-climbing. Verified: fixture where cycle-2→3 delta < epsilon reports converged-stuck, a climbing sequence reports cap-reached.

title: External advisory lens: seat Codex as a displayed-but-uncounted reviewer in the consensus panel
idea: Flip 'the reviewer roster is Claude-only subagents' toward '100 heterogeneous reviewers including other engines' and pull back to the one defensible seat: an external engine (Codex) reviewing the same diff as a SHADOW lens whose score is displayed in the cycle table but never enters the pass denominator or the fix-routing gate. The 15/17 independent-synthesis convergence is direct evidence the second engine catches real things; seating it advisory-only harvests that signal without letting it gate. This explicitly engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) revisit-when: it does NOT add an external-engine gating slot — it is the chaperone-dispatch 'second-opinion→opus/high' shape from #318 applied to review, an advisory participant whose verdict Claude, the verifier-of-record, may adopt or discard. The score column is annotated 'advisory, not counted' so the governance boundary is legible in the artifact itself.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons + §3 finding 2: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' — named prior art living in the session-mining synthesis (wf_7e5d77a2-5c0); the chaperone-dispatch second-opinion shape already exists at plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md, giving a home for an advisory-review worker without inventing a new executor kind.
outcome_shape: PR adding an 'advisory reviewer' row-type to consensus-protocol.md's score-display + Step B3 (explicitly excluded from the >=9.0 denominator and re-review routing) and an external-engine-workers.md entry for a second-opinion review worker; test asserts an advisory reviewer's score never changes the consensus verdict. Verified by a fixture where a 4.0 advisory score leaves an otherwise-passing panel PASS.

title: Diff-shaped lens selection: port saga /code-review's judgment-selected lenses into team-execution's fixed roster
idea: Flip the fixed 5-dimension reviewer roster to the '100 possible lenses' extreme and mine the routing intelligence. team-execution spawns a static reviewer set regardless of what the diff touches (a pure-docs diff still summons the security and infra reviewers, who then score inert dimensions), while saga /code-review already selects lenses by judgment against the actual diff. Port that selection: a lens-selection step that reads the diff shape from the reviewer-registry and seats only applicable reviewers, recording the excluded ones as 'not-seated' with a cause — the same static-non-applicable vocabulary consensus-protocol.md already uses for excluded dimensions, lifted from dimension-granular to reviewer-granular. Consensus membership becomes portable and diff-appropriate rather than a fixed list, and the denominator honesty the protocol already prizes extends to who is even in the room.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:82-108 already defines 'static-non-applicable' exclusion but ONLY dimension-granular within one reviewer, explicitly noting a whole-lens exclusion path (':93-94, a reviewer whose entire lens is non-applicable is excluded WHOLE'); reviewer-registry.md exists as the seat roster and saga/code-review/SKILL.md already does judgment-selected lenses against the diff — the selection intelligence exists in one plugin and is absent in the other.
outcome_shape: PR adding a lens-selection step to consensus-protocol.md Step B3a keyed to reviewer-registry.md diff-shape tags, emitting a 'not-seated (static-non-applicable)' line per excluded reviewer; test asserts a docs-only diff seats no code-surface reviewers and the consensus denominator reflects only seated lenses. Verified by a docs-diff fixture producing a reduced, honestly-named panel.

title: Consensus-worthiness gate: a $0-consensus flip that decides when the panel is worth its tokens
idea: Flip the token budget to $0: if consensus could never spend a token, what would you still run? A single-reviewer smoke pass. That extreme exposes that team-execution today runs the full multi-reviewer 3-cycle panel unconditionally, even on a one-line typo fix — the 350-450k-tokens-in-20-min recon number shows how fast fan-out spend compounds. Add a consensus-worthiness predicate that sizes the panel to the change: below a diff-size/risk floor, run a single consolidated reviewer (or skip to advisory) and escalate to the full gated panel only when risk signals (security/auth/infra/cross-repo touch, or diff above a threshold) fire. The escalation ladder is the kernel — it makes 'when is consensus worth it' an explicit, tuned decision rather than an always-on cost, and it reuses the exact risk signals the governance-split router already computes.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)' quantifies fan-out cost; operator-choice.md:97-104 already computes the risk signals (has_security, has_infra, cross_repo, deployment_sensitive) that would key the escalation floor — the inputs exist, they are just never used to right-size the consensus panel, which always runs full per consensus-protocol.md Step B3.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus-worthiness section to consensus-protocol.md (Step B3-pre) keyed to the existing risk signals + a diff-size floor, defining single-reviewer / advisory / full-gated-panel tiers with escalation triggers; test asserts a sub-floor no-risk diff routes to single-reviewer and any security-touch diff forces the full panel. Verified by paired fixtures (trivial docs diff vs auth-touching diff).

title: Byzantine-quorum weighting for cross-engine consensus review
idea: Distributed consensus (PBFT / weighted quorum) tolerates faulty nodes by weighting votes and requiring a supermajority, not naive unanimity. Consensus review currently reconciles Claude+Codex by hand (15/17 convergence). Formalize a portable quorum protocol: each reviewer emits typed findings with a confidence weight; agreement above a quorum threshold auto-confirms, disagreements surface as the reconcile set for Claude (verifier-of-record) to adjudicate. This makes the 15/17 hand-reconciliation mechanical and portable across engines while keeping external engines advisory-only.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' and §3 finding 2 (consensus catching defects green suites missed). Engages binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} — quorum is advisory input; Claude adjudicates the disagreement set, preserving verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: Merged consensus-quorum protocol spec + reference implementation in team-execution that emits an auto-confirmed set and a Claude-adjudication set, with a fixture reproducing the 15/17 split.

title: Consensus elasticity: shrink panels where measured reviewer agreement is high, backed by sampled spot-checks
idea: Flip consensus to zero — one reviewer everywhere — and ask where that is actually safe. The uncomfortable answer: nobody knows, because the fleet never measures reviewer agreement; panel sizes are set by convention, and the operator-praised defect catches may be concentrated in a minority of lens/file-type combinations while the rest is over-provisioned ceremony. Kernel: team-execution records per-review agreement (findings overlap between panel members, echoing the hand-reconciled 15/17 Claude+Codex convergence) into a ledger; where a lens shows sustained near-unanimity, panel size drops to one with a sampled second reviewer as a spot-check, and any spot-check disagreement snaps the lens back to full panel. Gated decisions remain Claude-verified throughout, so never-gatekeepers is untouched — this resizes Claude-internal panels, not the advisory/gated split.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 singleton: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' — an 88% agreement rate measured once by hand is exactly the signal proposed for systematic capture; section 3 item 2 (consensus review catching defects green suites missed, 2 repos, operator-praised) supplies the counter-pressure the spot-check snap-back mechanism answers. {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} engaged: elasticity applies only to Claude-internal panel sizing.
outcome_shape: Merged: an agreement-ledger written by team-execution's consensus step plus a documented panel-sizing policy consuming it, with snap-back rules and an initial report from historical review artifacts.
dod_sketch: Merged: an agreement-ledger written by the consensus step + a panel-sizing policy that shrinks panels where measured agreement is high with sampled spot-check snap-back; test asserts a spot-check disagreement reverts the lens to full panel.

title: Consensus Treaty Files
idea: Extract consensus rules into portable "treaty" profiles covering quorum, independence requirement, allowed providers, disagreement handling, confidence scoring, and gate/advisory behavior, so team-execution, saga review, Codex rescue, and external reviewers all consume the same profile rather than carrying hardcoded thresholds; historical Claude+Codex convergence becomes calibration data instead of folklore.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: consensus is a protocol; burying it inside one plugin prevents reuse and calibration.

title: Portable consensus kernel: typed gated/advisory bit, worthiness entry gate, and a non-scoring external seat
idea: Extract the consensus machinery once with its three strongest amendments built into the contract rather than bolted on: T5-F6-1's single versioned scoring spec (consensus_spec.py, deleting prose-as-source-of-truth and the ~24 hand-copied threshold constants), T5-F4-3's gated-vs-advisory governance bit stamped on every verdict artifact so porting cannot leak the boundary, T5-F6-8's consensus-worthiness entry gate so a panel must earn its convene, and T5-F4-4's external-engine advisory seat — displayed, never counted — making the 15/17 Claude+Codex convergence a repeatable membership mode. Shipping the kernel without these three would immediately generate the amendment PRs; shipping them as contract fields makes /work and /outcome consumers correct by construction.
